bug_semantics: The Google Cloud Secret Manager secrets backend in Apache Airflow's Google provider (providers/google/.../cloud/secrets/secret_manager.py) accepted a `team_name` parameter on `get_conn_value` and `get_variable` but dropped it at the internal call boundary: both methods delegated to `_get_secret(path_prefix, secret_id)`, a helper with no team parameter, so every lookup built the team-agnostic secret name regardless of the caller's team. In a deployment running multi-team mode with this backend, a task or Dag belonging to one team resolved another team's Connection or Variable and obtained its credentials in full (CWE-1220 Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key / CWE-863 Incorrect Authorization).
flaw_origin: Commit a4f3417bb0ae22a447b974e5e543af45e55e3c7f ("Check team boundaries in connections (#59476)", 2026-01-05, author Vincent <97131062+vincbeck@users.noreply.github.com>, committer GitHub) — with its variables twin d32091cd4f4b ("Check team boundaries in variables (#58905)", 2025-12-10, same author) — added the `team_name: str | None = None` parameter to `get_conn_value`/`get_variable` of the Google backend but left the delegation `return self._get_secret(self.connections_prefix, conn_id)` / `return self._get_secret(self.variables_prefix, key)` unchanged: the team argument was accepted and silently discarded, giving multi-team deployments the appearance of team-scoped resolution without any. The underlying team-agnostic `_get_secret` design predates teams (introduced with the variables interface by 0e1c238b2fff, 2020-03-28, Kaxil Naik, #7946), so at team-boundary time the backend was still team-agnostic by design; the flaw that matters for the advisory — team_name accepted-but-dropped — is born at a4f3417bb0ae/d32091cd4f4b.
